beats.trigger: ## Security
beats.got: nothing new; a title.

beats.trigger: It is important to involve the right stakeholders early, to follow best practices, and to keep iterating as the landscape changes.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Read the [Agent Trigger List, After Module 3]
beats.got: Homework with three links and no stated cost in hours.

beats.trigger: **Evaluate** residual risk: what is left, and what future sessions need before touching the system
beats.got: A list of verbs. 'Residual risk' is at least a term I know.

beats.trigger: Name what you'd want to check before letting this near a real stakeholder.
beats.got: A fair question. I'd start with where the data goes and who approved the tool.

beats.trigger: A tool call is text crossing a boundary into action.
beats.got: The agent writes a request and software executes it. Clearer than I expected, but no cost or risk figure.

beats.trigger: Leading companies are investing in enablement programmes, champions networks and training, and the ones that start early will be best placed.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: You find the bug, fix it, and check that the fix holds.
beats.got: Normal software behaves the same each time, so the old controls work.

beats.trigger: One passing test is one sample.
beats.got: An agent can pass an audit once and fail the next day, and an attacker can steer it with plain English in a document. That is a control problem I can understand.

beats.trigger: Remember that success with AI is everyone's responsibility.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: This is a rapidly evolving area, and organisations of every size are working out how best to approach it.
beats.got: nothing new; the same paragraph again.

beats.trigger: More context makes a good answer likelier. Less access makes a bad answer smaller.
beats.got: Limit what it can touch, and sign for what is left.

beats.trigger: Expect it to cost you a feature.
beats.got: Not opening a door is the cheapest control, and it has a price I can weigh. This is the first thing I could put in front of the board.

beats.trigger: Industry analysts expect agent adoption to accelerate significantly over the coming years.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: **Time:** 40 minutes. Phase 1 ~10, Phase 2 ~8, Phase 3 ~22.
beats.got: Forty minutes on a system built in earlier modules that I haven't seen. It is not my material.

beats.trigger: Read the first few rows: they show which rules files can check and which need judgment, context, or a standing evidence check.
beats.got: The agent splits rules into checkable and needs-judgment. I'd want to see the report.

beats.trigger: the data your agent touches that would be a problem if it leaked
beats.got: I'd name the finance data and the unreleased numbers. That is my material, finally.

beats.trigger: Expect many questions; the agent keeps probing both lenses over several rounds.
beats.got: Twenty-two minutes of the agent interviewing me. Long.

beats.trigger: *"You choose. Optimise for what I can't steer."*
beats.got: I can hand the rest back to the agent. Fine, but I'd need someone to check what it chose.

beats.trigger: Run `ls .claude/skills/agent-audit/` to confirm.
beats.got: File-system mechanics. That is for my IT people.

beats.trigger: Agent mitigations sit on top of normal company controls, not in place of them.
beats.got: The agent check adds to our ISMS and doesn't replace it. That settles one objection.

beats.trigger: Clear communication, strong sponsorship and regular follow-up remain the foundation
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Type `/` and look for `/agent-audit` in the autocomplete list.
beats.got: The saved check shows up as a command. Quick.

beats.trigger: Expect the reusable check to find things you did not think about, and to leave things "I can't tell" you thought were settled.
beats.got: A report with compliant, violating and can't-tell rows is something I can read like an audit finding. 'Can't tell' is honest.

beats.trigger: The uncomfortable feeling is the evidence.
beats.got: A ranked risk list. 'Uncomfortable feeling is evidence' is a feelings line, not a figure.

beats.trigger: It is important to involve the right stakeholders early, to follow best practices
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The narrow question the expert can answer is sitting in the report. Walk in with that.
beats.got: Take the report and the one open question to legal or IT. That is how I'd get the finance-data approval.

beats.trigger: Risk control, done for every risk you found, separates a prototype from a production agent.
beats.got: One risk handled is a demo. All of them is production. No hours given, but the logic is sound.

beats.trigger: the ones that start early will be best placed.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The agent reviews the audit session and adds one to five rules to the root instructions file for future sessions.
beats.got: The agent writes its own rules for next time. Useful, if someone reviews them.

beats.trigger: A skill is not a deployed service and does not settle ownership.
beats.got: A skill is a shareable method, not a product. I notice it says nothing on who owns it.

beats.trigger: agents are simply one more area where those principles apply.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: "the missing organisational check was X."
beats.got: One sentence per case, and a check is something I understand. Fine. The last line is a bit pushy.

beats.trigger: Read Mata v. Avianca (2023) and Deloitte Australia / DEWR report (2025) in the lecture.
beats.got: Two real cases where output went out unchecked, one a Big Four refund. That is the kind of evidence I respect.

take_homes: Not opening a door is the cheapest control. It costs a feature, and I can price that.
An agent audit is a report of compliant, violating and can't-tell rows, so I can ask for one and read it. It sits on top of our existing controls.
When the report has an open item, take the report and one narrow question to legal or IT.

monday.move: Ask IT and legal one question: may an agent read finance data, and what is the minimum access scope? Ask whoever built the system for the can't-tell report.
monday.stop_condition: If they won't approve any finance-data access, I stop and do nothing until they do.
monday.blocker: IT hasn't approved the tool for finance data. The whole module assumed a system I didn't build, so I have nothing to run it on.

misconception.why: I still think of AI as a licence you buy, but the module showed that someone has to define and keep checking the limits, so the work is ongoing and in-house. I still don't have a cost figure.

one_line: Four paragraphs of consultant filler, but the door-you-don't-open idea and the audit report are worth having. Cut the filler and give me a number.
